channel.title: Cadillac recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Cadillac Escalade IQ, Hummer EV Battery Fire Risk
item.description: Certain Cadillac Escalade IQ, Escalade IQL and GMC Hummer EV Pickup vehicles may have a problem with the high voltage battery. An internal component inside the battery may not be properly secured in place. If this component becomes loose, it can move around inside the battery and cause damage to it. Damage to the high voltage battery in this way increases the risk of a fire.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC SUVs Have Wrong Wheel Bolts
item.description: Some 2025 and 2026 Cadillac Escalade, Escalade ESV, Chevrolet Tahoe, GMC Yukon, and Yukon XL vehicles with 24-inch wheels may have the wrong bolts installed on the left and right front wheel hubs. Over time, these incorrect bolts can loosen or become deformed. This affects how securely the front wheels are held onto the vehicle, since the bolts holding them in place are not the correct type for these hubs.

item.title: GM vehicles may be missing the electronic owner's manual
item.description: General Motors is recalling a wide range of Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC and Buick vehicles, including the Escalade IQ and IQL, OPTIQ, Colorado, Equinox EV, Silverado 3500, Canyon and Sierra 3500. During production, the radio may not have been set to the correct status to download the electronic owner's manual, so the manual is not there for the owner to use. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard covering occupant protection.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC SUVs Rear Wheel Lockup
item.description: On these Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC SUVs equipped with a 10-speed automatic transmission, the transmission control valve may fail. If the valve fails, it can cause the rear wheels to lock up while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq Rearview Camera Screen May Go Gray
item.description: On some Cadillac Lyriq vehicles, the rearview camera screen may turn gray and stop showing any picture from the camera. Without that camera image, the driver loses the extra view behind the vehicle that the system is supposed to provide.

item.title: Cadillac Optiq, Equinox EV Tire Tread Detachment
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain 2025-2026 Cadillac Optiq and 2025-2026 Chevrolet Equinox EV vehicles that are equipped with 21-inch Continental all-season tires. On some of these vehicles, part of the tire's tread, or the entire tread, may separate from the tire while the vehicle is being driven. This is known as tread detachment and can affect one or more of the vehicle's tires.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevy, GMC SUVs Have Wrong Fuel Tank
item.description: Certain Cadillac Escalade, Chevrolet Tahoe, and GMC Yukon vehicles with a 6-cylinder diesel engine may have had their original fuel tank replaced with the wrong one. If that happened, fuel could leak out of the tank if the vehicle is involved in a rollover crash.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq Battery Bolts May Be Loose
item.description: Some Cadillac Lyriq and Vistiq vehicles may have loose or missing bolts holding the high-voltage battery to the floor of the vehicle.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq Driver Display Can Go Blank
item.description: The driver's video display may suddenly go blank while you're driving. That screen shows things like the speedometer, warning lights, and the rearview camera image, so losing it means losing that information while on the road. Dealers will update the display's software, or it can be updated automatically over the air, free of charge.

item.title: GM Trucks and SUVs Engine May Fail
item.description: Certain Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC trucks and SUVs with a 6.2L V8 gas engine may have manufacturing defects in the connecting rod and/or crankshaft. These defects can damage the engine and cause it to fail.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq Front Stabilizer Bar Bolts May Loosen
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Cadillac Lyriq vehicles. The bolts on the bracket that holds the left or right front stabilizer bar may not have been tightened properly. Over time, these bolts can loosen and allow the bracket to separate from the vehicle's frame. If that happens, the loose stabilizer bar or bracket can damage nearby high-voltage cables or the coolant lines for the EV battery.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq Owner's Manual Misdescribes Head Restraints
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain 2025 Cadillac LYRIQ vehicles because the owner's manual inaccurately describes the rear outboard head restraints. If an owner relies on this incorrect description, the head restraints may end up improperly adjusted, which increases the risk of injury in a crash.

item.title: GM Cars: Electric Power Steering Assist May Fail
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain 2016-2018 Cadillac CTS, 2017-2018 Cadillac ATS, Chevrolet Camaro, and Chevrolet Corvette vehicles. The electric power steering assist may fail while the vehicle is being driven. This power steering system normally helps reduce the effort needed to turn the steering wheel, and this recall covers vehicles where that assist can stop working.

item.title: Cadillac and Camaro Transmission May Lock Wheels
item.description: The 10-speed transmission in these vehicles may become damaged internally, and that damage can cause the wheels to lock up while driving. A wheel locking up while driving increases the risk of a crash. Dealers will install new monitoring software in the transmission's computer to address the problem, free of charge.

item.title: Diesel GM trucks, SUVs risk rear wheel lock-up
item.description: On certain diesel Chevrolet, GMC and Cadillac trucks and SUVs, the transmission control valve may fail. If it fails, the rear wheels can lock up while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Cadillac XT4 dashboard cover may block passenger airbag
item.description: The cover on the instrument panel may be missing a perforation on its underside that is needed for the passenger-side airbag to deploy properly.

item.title: GM SUVs, Trucks Brake Warning Light May Fail
item.description: Certain Chevrolet, GMC, and Cadillac SUVs and trucks may have a software problem in the brake control module. This software is supposed to turn on a warning light when the brake fluid level gets too low, but it may fail to do so. Because of this, a driver might not realize the brake fluid is low, since the vehicle isn't giving them the warning it's designed to show.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq Brakes May Release Pressure Unexpectedly
item.description: Some Cadillac Lyriq all-wheel-drive vehicles have an anti-lock brake system that can turn on by itself and let out brake pressure in the vehicle's brake system.

item.title: Cadillac XT4 and Malibu Wrong Owner's Manual
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain 2024 Cadillac XT4 and Chevrolet Malibu vehicles that may have the wrong owner's manual in the glove box. Because the manual doesn't match the vehicle, it can contain inaccurate information about how the vehicle's functions work and other safety-related details. Having incorrect information available to the driver could lead to the vehicle being operated the wrong way.

item.title: Cadillac XT5 and XT6 dashboard reminder lights may not work
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Cadillac XT5 and XT6 vehicles. On these cars, the instrument panel may not light up when the hazard warning lights, the high beams, or the turn signals are switched on, so the usual reminder on the dash is missing. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet two federal safety rules, one covering controls and displays and one covering lamps and reflectors. Dealers will update the instrument panel software.

item.title: GM Electric Vehicles May Lose Drive Power
item.description: In some 2024 Cadillac Lyriq, Chevrolet Blazer EV, Chevrolet Silverado EV, GMC Hummer EV, and GMC Sierra EV vehicles, the electric motors in the rear drive unit may have wires that aren't insulated well enough. If those wires touch each other, the vehicle can lose the power that drives it.

item.title: Cadillac XT5 driver airbag may not deploy
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain 2024 Cadillac XT5 vehicles because the driver's front air bag cushion may tear while the air bag is deploying. If the cushion tears, the air bag may not deploy the way it is designed to. An air bag that fails to deploy properly cannot provide the protection it is meant to give the driver during a crash.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq Rear Seat Belt Anchor May Fail
item.description: In some Cadillac LYRIQ vehicles, the bracket that holds the left-rear and center-rear seat belts to the seat frame may not have been welded correctly. Because of this, that bracket may not hold the seat belts as firmly as it should. A seat belt that isn't anchored securely may not keep a passenger properly restrained. This affects anyone riding in the left-rear or center-rear seating position.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq Recalled for Missing Pedestrian Warning Sounds
item.description: The body control module on some vehicles may have been updated with incorrectly calibrated software, causing it to fail to make the sounds meant to warn pedestrians that the vehicle is approaching.

item.title: Cadillac XT5, XT6 and GMC Acadia windshield problem
item.description: This recall affects certain GMC Acadia and Cadillac XT5 and XT6 vehicles. Some windshields may have been installed without the correct sealant needed to bond the glass to the vehicle's body. Without that seal, the windshield may not be properly attached, and it could come loose from the vehicle.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevrolet and GMC SUVs Rear Suspension Bolts May Break
item.description: The bolts that attach the rear outer control arm to the suspension may not have been heat-treated correctly. This can cause the bolts to break.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq Battery Pack Loss Of Power
item.description: Certain Cadillac Lyriq vehicles may have connections inside the high-voltage battery pack that are out of position or were not welded correctly. This problem can cause the vehicle to suddenly lose drive power while you are driving, meaning the car may stop being able to move forward or accelerate as expected. Losing power unexpectedly on the road can make it difficult to keep the vehicle moving safely, especially in traffic or at higher speeds.

item.title: Cadillac, Chevy, GMC SUVs Transmission Half-Shaft Failure
item.description: Certain Cadillac XT5, XT6, Chevrolet Blazer, Traverse and GMC Acadia SUVs may have been built with an incorrect transmission part called a sun gear. This can cause the half-shaft on the driver's side to come loose from the transmission.

item.title: Cadillac XT5, GMC Acadia Half-Shaft Can Separate
item.description: On affected vehicles, the right-front half-shaft — part of what sends power from the engine to the wheel — may not be properly connected to the transmission. This can cause the half-shaft to separate. If that happens, the vehicle can lose the power that drives it forward, or the vehicle could roll away on its own after being put in park.

item.title: GM Vehicles Daytime Running Lights Stay On
item.description: In certain Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC vehicles, the daytime running lights may not turn off when the headlights are switched on. This can create glare and reduce visibility for other drivers.

item.title: Cadillac XT4 rearview camera image may go blank
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Cadillac XT4 SUVs that have the optional Surround Vision feature. The video processing module may lose its connection with the rearview camera, and the camera image is then lost. Dealers will update the module's software, or replace the module if needed.

item.title: GM SUVs: Daytime Running Lights May Not Turn Off
item.description: On some Cadillac Escalade and Escalade ESV, Chevrolet Tahoe and Suburban, and GMC Yukon and Yukon XL vehicles, the daytime running lights may not turn off when the headlights are on. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet a federal safety lighting standard.

item.title: Cadillac and GMC label with unreadable tire size information
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain 2023 Cadillac XT5 and XT6 and GMC Acadia vehicles. The certification label on the driver's side B-pillar, the post between the front and rear doors, may have tire size information on it that cannot be read. Because of that, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule that covers how tires and rims are chosen for a vehicle. Dealers will put on a new certification label.

item.title: Cadillac XT5, XT6, GMC Acadia Camera May Fail
item.description: On vehicles with the optional Surround Vision feature, the coaxial cable connectors for the rearview camera may have been crimped incorrectly. This can cause the rearview camera to stop working or work only some of the time.

item.title: Cadillac Lyriq Instrument Panel May Go Blank
item.description: General Motors says a software error in the driver video display control module on some Cadillac Lyriq vehicles may cause the instrument panel to go blank. When this happens, the panel would not show information like your speed and warning lights. GM is recalling the affected vehicles to fix this software error in the display control module.

item.title: GM SUVs Third-Row Seat Belt Buckle Rivet Flaw
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Cadillac Escalade, Escalade ESV, Chevrolet Suburban, Tahoe, GMC Yukon, and Yukon XL vehicles with third-row seats. The rivet that holds the buckle to its mounting bracket in the left or right third-row seat belt buckle may have been improperly formed. A seat belt with a deformed rivet may not properly restrain a passenger. Dealers will inspect the rivet on both third-row seat belt buckles and replace the buckle assemblies if needed, at no cost.

item.title: Cadillac XT5/XT6 and GMC Acadia Fuel Tank Valve Leak
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Cadillac XT5, XT6, and GMC Acadia All-Wheel Drive vehicles. A valve inside the fuel tank, meant to seal the tank shut if the vehicle rolls over, may not seal properly. If that valve fails to seal during a rollover crash, fuel can leak out of the tank. A fuel leak like this raises the chance of a fire starting after the crash.

item.title: Cadillac XT5, XT6, GMC Acadia Rear Suspension Link May Separate
item.description: On some of these vehicles, a part called the toe link connects to the left-rear suspension and helps keep the rear wheel aligned. That toe link may not have been tightened properly when the vehicle was built. If it stays loose, the toe link could become loose or come apart from the suspension instead of staying securely attached the way it should be.

item.title: Cadillac XT6 brake fluid cap missing warning label
item.description: On certain 2022 Cadillac XT6 vehicles, the cap on the brake fluid reservoir may be missing its warning label. Because the label is missing, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule for light vehicle brake systems. Dealers will look at the brake fluid reservoir cap and replace it if needed. General Motors mailed notification letters to owners at the end of June 2022.

item.title: GM Vehicles: Driver's Seat Weld May Fail
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain 2021 Chevrolet Malibu and 2022 Chevrolet Equinox, Blazer, and Cadillac XT4 vehicles. The driver's seat cushion frame may have a weld that was not done correctly. This faulty weld is located in the power tilt-adjustment mechanism, which is the part that lets the driver's seat tilt up and down. The improper weld affects the frame that supports the driver's seat cushion.
